# The Days of Duveen

A legendary art dealer and his clients.

By S. N. Behrman

September 22, 1951

Illustration by Saul Steinberg

(This is the first of a series of articles on Lord Duveen. Read the last part.)

When Joseph Duveen, the most spectacular art dealer of all time, travelled from one to another of his three galleries, in Paris, New York, and London, his business, including a certain amount of his stock in trade, travelled with him.

# S. N. Behrman

## The Days of Duveen—V: The Blue Boy and Two Lavinias

 How Joseph Duveen flattered Arabella and Henry Huntington into buying Gainsborough’s “Blue Boy,” two Lavinias, and much more. 

October 20, 1951

## The Days of Duveen—IV: B. B.

 As Bernard Berenson shaped American taste from his Tuscan villa, the scholar’s alliance with Joseph Duveen remade—and scarred—the art world. 

October 13, 1951

## The Days of Duveen—III: A Brisk Market in Immortality

 Joseph Duveen turned raw American fortunes into Old Master collections—and competitive bids for cultural immortality. 

October 6, 1951

## The Days of Duveen—II: A Beginning in Delft

 From a Dutch blacksmith’s forge to Fifth Avenue showrooms, Joseph Duveen and Uncle Henry transform family delft into global art power. 

September 29, 1951

## The Days of Duveen

A legendary art dealer and his clients.

September 22, 1951
